findings.title: Success-criteria grep and site counts are inconsistent and cannot pass as written
findings.description:
The architecture requires each maintenance slice to have clear success criteria; the central functional criterion here fails on its own terms.

- **Line-number filter is a no-op.** The command uses `grep -roE` without `-n`, so output is `path:match` with no line numbers. The filter `grep -v 'introspection/types.ts:[3-6]:'` therefore removes nothing, and the four `STATUS` definition literals always match. Even with `-n`, hard-coded lines 3-6 break on any edit above them.
- **"Zero matches in the six swept files" contradicts the exclusions.** The design keeps the 3 quoted alias keys in `statusNormalizer.ts` (lines 34, 48) and the `'complete'` member of `SliceStatus.status` in `types.ts` (line 49). Both are in swept files and both still match.
- **The "After" count omits survivors.** Line 151 lists 4 + 3 + 4 remaining literals but leaves out the 3 `statusNormalizer.ts` alias keys.
- **The numbers do not add up.**
  - Line 35 says `types.ts` has "5 (of 8 total; 4 are the `STATUS` definition)", but 8 − 4 = 4, and the `inferredStatus` union at line 43 has only 3 literals.
  - Line 150 says "8 out-of-scope sites" while line 151 itemises 3 + 4 = 7.
  - Line 151 gives 4 `SliceStatus.status` sites, but the union at line 49 contains one overlapping literal.
  - The "~65" total at line 41 inherits the `types.ts` error.

Fix: state the counts once, in the scope table, and have the other sections reference it. Replace the grep criterion with an explicit allow-list of expected survivors (file plus reason), matched on content rather than line number.

findings.title: No rule for distinguishing NormalizedStatus sites from SliceStatus.status sites that share the spelling 'complete'
findings.description:
TD-3 excludes `SliceStatus.status` because sweeping it "implies the two unions are related, which they aren't". That exclusion is only stated for the type declaration in `types.ts`. The swept files `WorkflowNavigator.ts` and `ConsistencyChecker.ts` are consumers of slice workflow status, and the scope table (lines 33, 36) describes their sites only as `=== 'complete'` checks.

The compiler cannot catch a mis-sweep. `STATUS.Complete` has literal type `'complete'`, so `sliceStatus.status === STATUS.Complete` type-checks and behaves identically. The build, the test suite and the typo spot-check at line 153 all pass on a wrongly swept site.

The line-151 figure of 4 `SliceStatus.status` survivors suggests such comparison sites exist outside `types.ts`, but the design never says where.

Fix: add a per-site rule (sweep only where the operand's declared type is `NormalizedStatus`) and list the `SliceStatus.status` comparison sites that must stay literal, by file. This also resolves the count ambiguity above.

findings.title: TD-1 widens an exported type while the Migration Plan says no public API signature changes
findings.description:
Retyping `TaskFileResult.inferredStatus` to `NormalizedStatus` (lines 43, 98) adds `'deprecated'` to an exported field's type. Any exhaustive `switch` or `Record` keyed on that field in the cli or mcp packages would then fail to compile.

Step 6 (`pnpm -r build`) would catch this, so it does not block. Either reword line 84 to acknowledge the widening, or use `Exclude<NormalizedStatus, typeof STATUS.Deprecated>`, which removes the duplicate definition without widening.

findings.title: Repeated sections can be trimmed
findings.description:
For a find-and-replace slice, the same content appears several times:

- The Component Structure table (lines 70-78) repeats the scope table (lines 31-39).
- TD-2 and TD-3 (lines 100-106) repeat the Excluded bullets (lines 47, 49).
- "Deferred to Other Slices" (lines 128-129) repeats them a third time.
- Walkthrough step 4 (lines 160-165) adds nothing beyond step 3 for a change that keeps values identical.

This duplication is how the counts drifted. Cut the Component Structure table, fold TD-2 and TD-3 into the Excluded bullets, and drop walkthrough step 4.
